claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The landing location was the Pacific Ocean approximately 60 miles off the coast of San Diego, CA.
The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha shortly after splashing down.
Recovery teams secured the capsule following the splashdown.
Recovery teams extracted the crew following the splashdown.
Recovery teams conducted initial medical evaluations following the splashdown.
Recovery teams returned to port after conducting initial medical evaluations.
NASA and the U.S. Navy conducted recovery efforts following the landing.
The Artemis II mission marked the return of the first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years.
